samples.question: A single thin dark trace crosses this sheet from its left end to its right end, and one straight blue reference line runs the whole width of the sheet. The trace has exactly one height at each horizontal position, so it can be followed end to end. Between its two ends the trace makes several separate bulges: each bulge leaves the blue line, swells to one side of it, and comes back to it, and the bulges are spread all the way across the sheet. For every bulge consider the area of paper trapped between the trace and the blue line. Add up the trapped areas of all bulges lying above the blue line, and separately add up the trapped areas of all bulges lying below it. Every bulge counts towards its own side, however wide or however tall it is, and a wide shallow bulge can trap more paper than a narrow deep one. The pale grey edge ticks and the pale coloured decoration are not part of the trace and carry no information. Which side traps more paper in total: above the blue line, or below it? Answer with the single word above or below.
